summary: A phase 2 platform trial tests a plethora of drug combinations that incorporate new agents ganfeborole and BTZ-043 and identifies two regimens for further clinical development.
title: New drugs for tuberculosis are put to the test

summary: Integrated clinical and wastewater monitoring during the 2024–2025 outbreaks of measles in South Africa enabled high-resolution tracking of virus spread and evolution. Whole-genome amplicon sequencing of wastewater samples revealed shifts in genotype prevalence, detailed transmission links and previously unreported interprovincial spread.
title: Wastewater sequencing enables scalable measles surveillance

summary: Measles outbreaks have surged globally, challenging surveillance and control efforts. In South Africa, the 2024−2025 measles outbreak led to nearly 4,000 reported cases, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign. However, tracking measles virus (MeV; species Morbillivirus hominis) transmission and evolution remains difficult at scale, particularly in settings with limited access to care, diagnostic testing and sequencing capacity. Wastewater can enable population-scale virus surveillance, but low MeV concentrations limit detection sensitivity and sequencing quality. Here we show that overcoming these technical challenges enables integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance that expands the coverage and resolution of MeV monitoring. We developed a virus concentration and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) workflow and applied it to 4,502 wastewater samples collected across all nine provinces of South Africa during the 2024−2025 outbreak. Wastewater MeV genotype prevalence tracked clinical estimates, and phylogenetic analyses combining wastewater and clinical sequences revealed geographically structured transmission and previously undetected inter-provincial spread. WGS recovered transmission links not captured by the field standard approach, which targets a 450-nucleotide region of the nucleoprotein gene (N450), highlighting the importance of WGS to accurately characterize transmission dynamics. Our study provides a cost-effective and scalable genomic surveillance approach to support measles control and elimination. Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analyses of wastewater and surveillance samples during the 2024−2025 measles outbreak in South Africa reveal previously undetected inter-provincial spread and transmission links, suggesting that wastewater-integrated whole-genome surveillance can improve measles monitoring and control efforts.
title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission

summary: The silicon microelectrode ‘Utah’ array has enabled people with paralysis to control computer cursors, operate prosthetic limbs and communicate using high-performance brain–computer interfaces. However, reports so far have typically been limited to one or two individuals, with no systematic assessment of array longevity, decoding accuracy and day-to-day stability. Here we present a comprehensive 20-year evaluation of neural data from the BrainGate clinical trials, spanning 2,289 recording sessions, 20 arrays and 14 participants. On average, arrays successfully recorded neural spiking waveforms on 35.6% of electrodes, with a modest 7 percentage point decline over the recording period (up to 7.3 years). Using a ‘decoding signal-to-noise ratio’ (dSNR) metric, we found that 11 of 14 arrays provided meaningful movement decoding throughout participation (median dSNR >1), with three achieving >70% accuracy compared with able-bodied mouse control. We also found that dSNR increased approximately logarithmically with the number of electrodes, providing a pathway for scaling performance. While longevity exceeded previous nonhuman primate studies, achieving peak performance consistently may require further improvements. Utah arrays recorded stable spiking activity for up to 7.3 years, with modest signal decline on average and sustained movement decoding in the majority of arrays analyzed, demonstrating the long-term feasibility of intracortical brain–computer interfaces.
title: Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain–computer interfaces over a 20-year period

summary: In a phase 3 study, children with obesity lost significantly more weight with semaglutide than with placebo, with more than one third achieving a body mass index below the threshold for obesity.
title: STEP Young trial shows semaglutide benefits in children
Author Correction: On-premise medical AI agents for reliable clinical decision-making

summary: Dementia risk at any age has been falling for decades. An analysis of ~219,000 people followed for up to 30 years shows that newer generations start old age with a larger cognitive capacity that declines more slowly than that of previous generations, and this combined advantage is large enough to account for the fall in dementia incidence.
title: Later-born generations have better memory and lose it more slowly
Publisher Correction: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
